description: The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Initial Accuracy, and Δ Accuracy—for a large language model’s response to external feedback, as studied in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from 0.86 to 1.00 on a linear scale, with tick marks at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale, with major ticks every 0.2. The blue solid line with circle markers represents “Final Accuracy,” which remains consistently high across the range, starting at approximately 0.92 at 0.86 initial confidence, peaking near 0.99 at 0.97, and ending at 0.98 at 1.00. The green dashed line with square markers, “Initial Accuracy,” begins at 0.65 at 0.86, rises gradually to 0.90 at 0.97, then dips to 0.77 at 1.00. The orange dashed line with diamond markers, “Δ Accuracy” (the difference between final and initial accuracy), starts at 0.27 at 0.86, declines to a low of 0.05 at 0.95, then rises sharply to 0.22 at 1.00. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability in measurements, with larger error bars observed for Δ Accuracy at lower initial confidence values.
